title: Covariance to correlation
instructions: Convert the covariance matrix into a correlation matrix by dividing by pairwise standard deviations.
hint: Work inside out. Extract asset variances from covariance diagonal.

explanation.meaning: Extract asset variances from covariance diagonal.
For every asset pair multiply the two variances, forming a matrix.
Divide covariance_ij by sigma_i*sigma_j, giving 1 on the diagonal.

title: Covariance eigenvalues
instructions: Return eigenvalues of the symmetric covariance matrix ordered largest to smallest.
hint: Work inside out. Use a symmetric-matrix eigensolver; the eigenvalues arrive sorted in ascending order.

explanation.meaning: Use a symmetric-matrix eigensolver; the eigenvalues arrive sorted in ascending order.
-1]::Reverse the 1D eigenvalue vector to order principal risk directions from largest to smallest.

title: Precision matrix
instructions: Compute the precision matrix by solving Sigma × X = Identity, rather than explicitly calling inv.
hint: Work inside out. Construct an identity right-hand side matching covariance dimension.

explanation.meaning: Construct an identity right-hand side matching covariance dimension.
Solve all columns simultaneously for X such that Sigma@X=I; often preferable to forming inv in production.

title: Volatility vector
instructions: Return a 1D vector of the standard deviations implied by the covariance matrix diagonal.
hint: Work inside out. Extract variances for each asset.

explanation.meaning: Extract variances for each asset.
Convert variance to standard deviation. The resulting vector has length equal to number of assets.

title: Covariance conditioning
instructions: First convert covariance into correlation, then return the 2-norm condition number of the correlation matrix.
hint: Work inside out. Convert asset variances into pairwise volatility products.

explanation.meaning: Convert asset variances into pairwise volatility products.
Normalize Sigma into an asset correlation matrix with ones on the diagonal.
Measure numerical conditioning of the correlation matrix, relevant for stable inversion.

title: Linear factor regression
instructions: Fit linear least-squares factor coefficients from columns 0–2 to target column 3, with no intercept. Return the coefficient vector.
hint: Work inside out. Use the first three columns as the feature design matrix X.

explanation.meaning: Use the first three columns as the feature design matrix X.
Use the fourth column as the response vector y.
Solve min squared residual norm of X beta - y and extract beta from the tuple returned by NumPy.

title: Regression fitted responses
instructions: Fit least-squares weights with the first three columns predicting the last column, then return all fitted y values.
hint: Work inside out. Estimate the coefficient vector from the observed features and response.

explanation.meaning: Estimate the coefficient vector from the observed features and response.
Apply matrix multiplication to obtain a fitted value for each observation.

title: Regression residual vector
instructions: Compute y minus fitted y for the three-factor least-squares model, as a 1D NumPy array.
hint: Work inside out. Fit the factor coefficients.

explanation.meaning: Fit the factor coefficients.
Generate in-sample fitted responses.
Return regression residuals aligned with observations.

title: Column-standardized features
instructions: Return all four columns standardized to mean 0 and population standard deviation 1.
hint: Work inside out. Compute one center and scale per feature column.

explanation.meaning: Compute one center and scale per feature column.
Normalize every column independently; the output keeps the original matrix dimensions.

title: Feature Gram matrix
instructions: Return X-transpose times X for the first three feature columns.
hint: Work inside out. Select X with n samples and 3 predictor columns.

explanation.meaning: Select X with n samples and 3 predictor columns.
Take the matrix product of transposed features with features, creating a 3-by-3 Gram matrix.

title: Leading factor direction
instructions: Return the first right-singular vector of the centered first three feature columns.
hint: Work inside out. Remove the mean from each predictor before PCA-like decomposition.

explanation.meaning: Remove the mean from each predictor before PCA-like decomposition.
Obtain V-transpose, whose rows are principal loading directions.
Select the leading right-singular vector; its sign is arbitrary in theory but deterministically fixed by the solver for this target.

title: Path feature L2 norms
instructions: Return the Euclidean norm of the first three feature columns for each row.
hint: Work inside out. Take three coordinates for every observation.

explanation.meaning: Take three coordinates for every observation.
Compute sqrt(sum(x_i²)) within each row, obtaining one norm per observation.

title: Quadratic covariance contraction
instructions: For an equal-weight vector across assets, return its covariance quadratic form wᵀΣw as a scalar using einsum.
hint: Work inside out. Create equal portfolio weights across all n assets.

explanation.meaning: Create equal portfolio weights across all n assets.
Contract two weight vectors with the covariance matrix; output is a scalar portfolio variance.

title: Covariance Cholesky factor
instructions: Normalize covariance to correlation, then return its lower-triangular Cholesky factor.
hint: Work inside out. Build all sigma_i*sigma_j products from diagonal covariance entries.

explanation.meaning: Build all sigma_i*sigma_j products from diagonal covariance entries.
Form the correlation matrix by normalizing covariance values.
Factor the positive definite correlation matrix as L@L.T, useful for correlated Monte Carlo shocks.

title: Find largest feature magnitude
instructions: For every row, return the value from columns 0–2 having the largest absolute magnitude, preserving the sign as a 1D array.
hint: Work inside out. Find the column POSITION of largest absolute feature per row; shape is (n,1).

explanation.meaning: Find the column POSITION of largest absolute feature per row; shape is (n,1).
Gather the ORIGINAL signed value at each row-specific position.
Flatten the n-by-1 result to the requested n-element vector.
